title: Reflective practice: turn experience into a next step
summary: Pause, describe what happened, test your interpretation and choose an action you can review.
takeaway: Separate what happened from your first interpretation, then choose an action you can review.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: These anecdotes and the SAVERS routine offer examples for personal reflection. Accounts of named people’s clothing choices are not independently checked explanations of brain energy. The leaf comparison is a metaphor; it does not establish a health outcome or one mandatory routine.

ranges.heading: A reflection cycle and space to reflect
ranges.introduction: Consider what happened, how you interpreted it, alternatives and your next action. Time, place, helpful people and internal resources can be prompts. A timed breathing pattern is supplied as a routine example; no medical benefit is claimed and it need not be used to complete the reflection.

title: Questions for purpose, contribution and strategic reflection
summary: Choose a question for the decision you face; record an answer, the evidence behind it and a next step.
takeaway: A relevant question needs an honest answer and a useful next step, rather than a score.

ranges.heading: Purpose across person, role and organization
Thresholds and the impulse to act

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: The boiling-point and escape-velocity questions are used as prompts, not specified scientific problems with enough conditions for one numerical answer. Ask what threshold, context and assumptions actually matter to your decision. The attributed action quotation is unverified.

ranges.heading: Life, contribution and achievements
ranges.introduction: Choose a small set of prompts that fit your situation. Business forecasts and personal values require different kinds of evidence and should not become one score.

ranges.heading: Values, relationships and future choices
ranges.introduction: Choose a small set of prompts that fit your situation. Business forecasts and personal values require different kinds of evidence and should not become one score.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: These examples connect ordinary life, reflection and sustained interest. The Gordon Mathews, Steve Jobs and Colin Powell quotations have not been independently authenticated as quoted. Use the reflection questions without treating an attributed sentence as proof.

ranges.heading: Four prompts: identity, proficiency, purpose and practice
ranges.introduction: These prompts concern self-reflection rather than a personality test: consider what matters, what you can do, how you want to contribute and what action comes next.

title: Learning and attention: deliberate practice without overload
summary: Break skills into learnable parts, protect attention and use feedback to revise the next attempt.
takeaway: Choose a consequential task, practise a manageable part and use feedback to revise the next attempt.

ranges.heading: Build a deliberate learning sequence
ranges.introduction: Select a skill, break it into chunks, sequence the prerequisites, connect it with prior knowledge and practise the consequential parts. “Dumping” is the source shorthand for prioritizing relevant information, not deleting evidence you still need.

ranges.heading: Attention, distractions and pressure
ranges.introduction: Choose a consequential task, distinguish attractive distractions from productive work and plan when to return after interruption. The source’s three-task rule and awareness chime are optional routines, not universal optimal thresholds.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: The source contrasts habitual/automatic activity with effortful planning and self-control. Treat this as a simplified explanatory model rather than two literal isolated brain systems. Use it to identify a task, likely interruption and the cue for returning.

title: Action and persistence: using maxims without becoming rigid
summary: Turn motivating sayings into testable habits while recognizing conflicts, constraints and reasons to change course.
takeaway: A useful maxim needs context, boundaries and a reason to revise the approach.

references.title: FranklinCovey's official book and habit guide

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: The Darwin attribution has not been verified. The useful reflection is to ask what evidence would make a plan change; a familiar attributed sentence is not proof of its authorship.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: Small reversible experiments can create learning opportunities; keep the cost and stopping conditions explicit. The attributed Gates, Sinek and Lincoln quotations remain unverified as quoted and should not establish a general rule about success or hiring.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: Use competence, integrity, relationships and commitment as discussion themes. “Success is never accidental” is an absolute maxim, not an evidence-based account of every successful outcome. The military analogy is illustrative.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: This list is attributed to an entrepreneurial set of maxims, not the Peter Principle about promotion. Persistence and initiative can be useful lenses, but ignoring rules, demanding perfection and pursuing many projects conflict with other source advice.

Translate a maxim into a bounded experiment: name the outcome, constraints, action, review date and stop/change conditions. Do not treat a motivational statement as permission to ignore safety, obligations or evidence.

ranges.heading: Trying an idea and personal agency

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: Try a bounded action and invite learning, while respecting real constraints. The “player/victim” contrast is motivational rhetoric, not a judgement of a person’s worth or circumstances.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: These are attributed or rhetorical reflections. The Einstein quotation has not been authenticated; neither statement establishes that persistence alone produces success.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: The readable themes are agency, feedback, preparation, courage, self-responsibility, boundaries and respect. Several shorthand phrases are unexplained; “Role charity” and “Kill nuclear reactor” cannot be confidently interpreted. They are retained as source ambiguities, not operational advice.

ranges.heading: Purpose, a plan and continued effort
ranges.introduction: The source links purpose and regular effort. Keep ambition compatible with rest, honest feedback, ethical constraints and a willingness to revise the plan.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: The notes emphasize decisive action, listening and testing ideas. Health, age and circumstances can be real constraints; the source’s dismissal of “excuses” should not encourage ignoring illness or blaming people for barriers.
Use specific actions and feedback to build confidence while staying open to evidence, support and a change of approach. The source’s claims about positive thought do not guarantee results.

ranges.heading: The action habit and a deliberate pause
ranges.introduction: Start a bounded action rather than waiting for perfect conditions. The source also recommends stepping back when stuck; persistence and a pause can be complementary choices, not competing universal laws.

ranges.heading: The supplied seven-habit reading
ranges.introduction: Compare the seven habits as a practice sequence: initiative, purpose, priorities, mutual benefit, understanding, cooperation and renewal. This short reference is not the complete book or an assessment of a person.

title: Reflective frameworks: purpose, needs and working preferences
summary: Use the supplied workstyle, purpose and needs lists as conversation prompts rather than predictions or fixed identities.
takeaway: Use a framework to ask better questions rather than fix a person’s identity.

ranges.heading: Working preferences and the millionaire sequence

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: Dynamo, Blaze, Tempo and Steel are supplied working-style labels, not a validated personality diagnosis. The numbered wealth-oriented sequence is a reflection list whose creator and predictive basis were not established.
Use the lists to ask what activities you enjoy, what help you need and which actions are within your control. They do not predict income, rank people or guarantee a route to wealth.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: The source offers labels for examining emotions, an informal pencil-release exercise and personal-development themes. Do not infer clinical effectiveness from the exercise or assume every bankruptcy or life change has a single psychological cause. The planning mnemonic is a reminder, not a guarantee.

ranges.heading: Seven needs and four Ikigai prompts

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: The seven labels and four purpose questions are supplied reflection frameworks. They are not established here as an exhaustive hierarchy, validated assessment or universal account of a tradition. Ask how the prompts fit your circumstances rather than forcing one ideal intersection.

title: Coaching and neuroscience claims: what the notes do not establish
summary: Separate practical reflection from unsupported brain mechanisms, hormone promises and prescribed emotional stages.
takeaway: A practical reflection exercise does not require an unverified brain mechanism.
notes: No treatment, clinical diagnosis, hormone intervention or prescribed grief timetable is provided here. Original assertions are retained as source material with their evidence limits.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: The six fear labels are not a diagnostic instrument. The source’s first grief list uses “blame”; another later list includes bargaining and adds resurgence. A person need not follow a fixed emotional sequence.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: The source provides no experiment or specified model for its RAS/consciousness explanation. Affirmations may be used as personal reminders; that does not verify the proposed brain mechanism or promise a health or success effect.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: The half-second timing formula and single-region account of willpower lack a supplied study, task or measurement method. They are not needed to practise pausing and making deliberate choices.

A larger replication did not reproduce the hormonal result associated with expansive posture. Do not promise a reliable testosterone change from a pose. The source’s other health and stress generalizations remain unverified, not treatment instructions.

ranges.heading: The resilience spiral is not a clinical pathway

review.status: Read the source with these limits

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: Grief responses can overlap, repeat or be absent. The source’s “resurgence” is not established here as a universal sixth stage. “Humans only learn through suffering” is an absolute philosophical claim, not a learning rule supported by the supplied material.

review.status: Read the source with these limits

review.status: Read the source with these limits

title: Power maxims: influence, incentives and ethical limits

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: Read the list as a study of influence and power rhetoric, not a code of conduct. Concealment, dependence, taking others’ credit and intimidation raise different ethical concerns from patience, focus or careful timing.

For any proposed tactic ask: whose informed choice is reduced, what duties apply, who bears the costs, and what transparent alternative could meet the legitimate objective? Keep the distinction between describing a tactic and endorsing it.

review.status: Read the source with these limits

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: The source mixes accountability ideas with guilt, surveillance cues, “gene pool,” submission and slavery metaphors. These do not become legitimate hiring or management policies because they appear in a business reading.
A constructive alternative is to agree roles, resources, review points, fair rewards and a safe way to raise concerns. Evaluate incentives without dehumanizing workers or encouraging dependency.

ranges.heading: Advice, failure and an inappropriate medical analogy

review.status: Read the source with these limits

The “cleopening” term describes a late-close/early-open schedule. It is not an endorsement of such scheduling. The productivity assertion about sociable telemarketers has no supplied study and should not become a universal judgement of workers.

Ask which risk can be reduced before committing, which uncertainty remains, and whether growth changes the competitive arena, cash needs or culture.

ranges.heading: The hedgehog questions

title: Quantum physics glossary: states, spin, barriers and open questions
summary: Connect the supplied technical terms with bounded explanations, and distinguish established models from proposed unification.
takeaway: Define the operator or physical model before interpreting a technical term.
notes: These definitions concern physics. They do not provide evidence for motivational claims about spiritual vibration, personal success or a business energy field.

MIT, Spin One-Half, Bras, Kets, and Operators, §2–3
Oregon State University, Time Evolution Refresher
MIT, Quantum Harmonic Oscillator, lecture 8, pp. 3–4 and 8–9
Rice University OpenStax, University Physics Vol. 3 §6.2

visuals.title: Keep the kinds of statement separate
rows: A physical framework with states, operators and measurement predictions
Research programmes beyond the supplied established models
Belief, metaphor or programme language; not validated by the glossary
visuals.note: A vocabulary comparison, not a claim of a completed theory of everything.

paragraphs: For an operator A, a nonzero state ψ satisfying Aψ = aψ is an eigenstate. For an observable, an ideal measurement in that state gives the corresponding value a; the term is relative to the specified operator.
The value a in Aψ = aψ is the eigenvalue associated with the eigenstate ψ. It is not restricted to a parameter in a differential equation.
A one-dimensional oscillator with potential V(x) = ½mω²x² has energy values Eₙ = ħω(n + ½), for n = 0, 1, 2, … . Its stationary states are not little particles following classical periodic paths.
In nonrelativistic quantum mechanics, iħ ∂ψ/∂t = Hψ describes how a state evolves under a Hamiltonian H. It is not a definition of wave–particle duality.
The operator representing energy and governing time evolution in the model. For a simple particle in a potential, H = p²/(2m) + V; more general systems have different Hamiltonians.

A beam of silver atoms separated into discrete components in a nonuniform magnetic field. The modern account relates the result to intrinsic spin; electron spin was a later interpretation, not the original experimenters’ starting explanation. Spin is not literal rotation of a small sphere.

Particles with half-integer spin and antisymmetric states under exchange of identical particles. Electrons are elementary examples; protons and neutrons are composite fermions. The category is not synonymous with elementary particle.

Particles with integer spin and symmetric states under exchange of identical particles. Photons are elementary examples, while pions are composite spin-zero bosons. Several identical bosons can occupy the same single-particle state.

Three dimensionless two-by-two matrices commonly used to represent spin-½ states. Spin components are ħ/2 times the corresponding Pauli matrix, so an unscaled matrix should not be called an angular momentum.

Solutions of the spherical Bessel differential equation, arising for example in radial wave problems. They relate to ordinary Bessel functions of half-integer order; spherical Bessel and spherical Neumann functions are distinct solution families.

Emission of electrons from a material after absorption of light with sufficient photon energy. In the elementary model, the maximum emitted kinetic energy is hν minus the work function; changing intensity alone does not replace the threshold-frequency condition.
For a position coordinate and its corresponding momentum component, Δx Δp ≥ ħ/2 relates the standard deviations of outcomes in a quantum state. It is more than ordinary instrument imprecision.

A particle can have a nonzero probability of transmission through a finite potential barrier even when its energy is below the barrier height. It is not specifically entry into an electrostatic field.

Diagrams used to organize terms in perturbative calculations of interactions. Their rules depend on the theory; they extend beyond a single photon and particle and are not literal tracks through space.

curatedBlocks.term: Standard Model, grand unification and quantum gravity
paragraphs: The Standard Model describes elementary particles and the electromagnetic, weak and strong interactions; it does not include gravity. A grand unified theory proposes a deeper unification beyond that model. Quantum gravity seeks a consistent quantum description of gravitation. An experimentally established theory of everything is not supplied by combining those labels.

A class of geometric spaces studied in mathematics and used in some string-theory compactifications. A compact space of six real dimensions is three complex dimensions; this does not mean “where the third dimension lies” or establish observed extra dimensions.

title: Spiritual reflection: desire, compassion, meaning and belief

takeaway: Keep a philosophical interpretation distinct from a factual claim about medicine or physics.

Read the spiritual interpretation separately from any proposed biological explanation; the brief list is not a clinical instrument.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: Faith and fear are used as spiritual/motivational categories. Claims about ego vibration or universal effects of faith are beliefs or metaphors here, not measured physical relationships.

Religious language and comments about knowing God are retained as interpretations. A statement about overcoming a feeling does not establish a clinical technique or require a reader to endorse one belief.

title: Entrepreneurial self-cultivation: a Chinese programme overview
summary: Read an English translation of the supplied Chinese overview, with its original text and missing programme details clearly distinguished.
takeaway: The supplied overview can be translated completely while its advertised five-, six- and seven-part systems remain unspecified.
notes: This is an attributed programme overview, not an independently validated development system. It announces five paths, six directions and seven levels without enumerating their contents; the eight audiences and nine business situations are supplied.
“Energy” and dimensional language are translated in philosophical or promotional context, not presented as measurable physical fields.

ranges.heading: Principles, business practice and the programme’s promise

pairs.original: 广明灯
pairs.english: Guangming Deng — the supplied programme title.

pairs.original: 一份生命的使用说明书
pairs.english: An instruction manual for life.

pairs.original: 既有企业持续健康发展的战略规划，更有个人生命成长的登顶规划。
pairs.english: A plan for the sustained, healthy development of an existing enterprise, together with a plan for reaching new heights in personal growth.

pairs.original: 如此，事业、家庭、成长，方向全方位合一，人生再无纠结和困惑。
pairs.english: In this way, career, family and growth are brought into alignment; the programme promises an end to inner conflict and confusion.

pairs.original: 以道驭术的三维学习空间
pairs.english: A three-dimensional learning space in which Dao—guiding principles—directs practical methods.

pairs.original: 中国企业界：中华民族从最初的“道”治，逐步演化成“法”治。企业同理，最高的是“道”治，再次制度文化，而今充斥在市场上的是各种企业管理的“术”、“器”。经济时代的30年，把“道”融会贯通于商业中的布道者微乎其微，近代企业管理的方法、工具大都从西方引入，与其说是治标不治本，不如说是学的都是形式，学不到背后精神的运作模式。忽略了背后的经商之道，走了多年断章取义的弯路，学了个形似而神不似，无“道”驾驭下的“法”和“术”如同不知根本病因就下药的治疗，结果可想而知。法的尽头是道。
pairs.english: The text argues that Chinese society moved from governance through Dao to governance through rules, and draws a parallel with business. It places guiding principles above systems and culture, and criticizes a market filled with techniques and tools. It says that few teachers in the past thirty years have integrated Dao with commerce, while imported Western methods are often copied in form without understanding their underlying spirit. It compares methods without an understanding of fundamentals to prescribing medicine without identifying the cause, concluding that the end point of rules is Dao.

pairs.original: 四海为家的能量加油站
pairs.english: An energy-refuelling station wherever one makes a home.

pairs.original: 当企业主内心见地及价值取向升华后，“学以致用”是必然选择——做一个践履所学的实践者，以自身及企业为载体，共同推动“生命的意义在于知晓生命真相，把握事物发展规律，奉献社会、利益他人”的价值观。余生和对的人，做对的事，持续成长。这是人和人之间心与心的紧密互动，顺便实现商业价值。
pairs.english: When business owners deepen their understanding and values, the text says that putting learning into practice follows naturally. It advocates using oneself and one’s enterprise to understand life, discern patterns, serve society and benefit others: spend the rest of life growing with the right people and doing the right things. It describes close human connection as the foundation, with commercial value following alongside it.

ranges.heading: Announced growth models and their missing details

pairs.original: 心灵成长的五大必经路径
pairs.english: Five necessary paths of spiritual growth.

pairs.original: 濒临绝境，用过太多的方法，又得不到任何有效的帮助和效果时，人才会把一直关注外在的眼睛回收，开发自己内心的力量。唯有陷入黑暗的境地，人才会不顾一切的追寻光明，如此迎来最伟大的高光时刻。
pairs.english: The text claims that when people reach a desperate situation, have tried many methods and found no effective help, they turn attention inward and develop inner strength. It presents the search for light in darkness as a route to a significant breakthrough.

pairs.original: 此心灵成长路径从企业主面临的具体问题中萃取智慧，如此，企业主方能不负曲折和困苦的经历，以煎熬为炉，炼出“火眼金睛”，明确企业乃至生命的方向。在教学相长、修身+践行的持续练习中，逐步登顶思想的高峰。
pairs.english: This proposed path draws lessons from the concrete problems faced by business owners. It treats difficulty and suffering as a furnace for developing discernment and clarifying the direction of the enterprise and of life. Through mutual learning, self-cultivation and sustained practice, it describes a gradual ascent toward a higher level of thought.

pairs.original: “蓦然回首”
pairs.english: Looking back suddenly.

pairs.original: 快意人生的六大修炼方向
pairs.english: Six directions of cultivation for a fulfilling life.

pairs.original: 跌不完的“跟头”、交不完的“学费”，起因就是抉择时只见其利不见其害，或只见其害不见其利。企业主看不到冬天过后的诗和远方，就是企业前行的最大障碍。无路可走的绝望本身，就是在困苦中磨练意志、韬光养晦的重要过程。经历过这种煎熬、磨炼，人才有机会顿悟——道在心中。
pairs.english: The text attributes repeated setbacks to seeing benefits without harms, or harms without benefits. It argues that an owner’s inability to see beyond a difficult period can obstruct the business. It presents despair and a period of quiet endurance as opportunities to strengthen resolve and eventually recognize Dao within the heart.

pairs.original: 本系统修心的六个维度，环环相扣，缺一不可，重在心法的修炼。心法和方法区别在于解决问题的维度不同。心法首先清晰的是：在人生的大局中，应该做什么？不应该做什么？什么是最重要的？什么是必要的。企业经营中精力应该专注什么？摒弃什么？选择不做什么和选择做什么同等重要。而方法则是就具体事情要怎么做。实施步骤又是什么。
pairs.english: The system describes six interdependent dimensions of inner cultivation, emphasizing underlying principles. It distinguishes these from methods: principles address what should or should not be done, what matters most and what is necessary in the larger picture; methods address how a particular task is carried out. In business, choosing what not to do is presented as equally important as choosing what to do.

pairs.original: 商界认知的七级能量场
pairs.english: Seven levels of an “energy field” of business understanding.

pairs.original: 人和人之间本身就存在着不同层级的运行轨道，本相安无事，但人看不懂背后的本质，仅看外在的优势条件选择了和不同于自身维度空间的人紧密合作，首先不可逾越的就是强大的沟通障碍，鸡同鸭讲，对牛弹琴，始于口角，终于灾祸。
pairs.english: The text proposes that people operate on different levels or tracks. It warns that choosing close collaborators only by external advantages, without understanding deeper differences, can create severe communication barriers and conflict.

pairs.original: 很多企业主目前面临的麻烦，多数是在处理前期因战略抉择失误而遗留下来的问题，导致企业主精力始终被“救火”事宜所占据。
pairs.english: It claims that many business owners’ current problems mostly come from earlier strategic mistakes, leaving their attention absorbed by firefighting.

pairs.original: 此“模型”让您看透“事”和“情”中的一切矛盾以及人以群分的真相，并深度解码财富的构成成分，一个人此生所具备的财富，所做事业的大小、强弱均在此能量场中全部显现，起点决定终点。
pairs.english: The programme claims that its model can reveal contradictions in situations and relationships, explain why people group together and decode the components of wealth. It claims that the size and strength of a person’s business and wealth can be seen in this “energy field,” asserting that the starting point determines the destination.

pairs.original: 明白了人生的终极意义以及活法，才能够决定企业正确的做法，企业经营首先解决的是做什么、和谁做的问题。做什么错了，怎么做都是错。借助“外眼”，企业主在制定战略的时候，因看得明白真切，审时度势，在起点上避开纷扰，精力专注于发展，事业才得以真正扬帆起航、一帆风顺。
pairs.english: The text argues that understanding life’s meaning and one’s way of living precedes sound business choices. It prioritizes what to do and with whom, saying that execution cannot repair the wrong fundamental choice. It proposes an outside perspective to help owners assess circumstances, avoid distractions at the outset and focus on development.

pairs.original: 八大适用对象
pairs.english: Eight intended audiences.

pairs.original: 苦苦寻觅、多方探索, 试过所有的管理办法仍没有找到持续健康发展之道的企业主。
pairs.english: Business owners who have searched widely and tried every management approach without finding a path to sustained, healthy development.

pairs.original: 已经走过激情澎湃的创业期, 正在寻求突破转型期或上升期的企业主。
pairs.english: Owners who have passed the passionate startup stage and seek a breakthrough, transition or a new phase of growth.

pairs.original: 有远大抱负, 致力于利国利民的企业主。
pairs.english: Owners with far-reaching ambitions who want their work to benefit their country and other people.

pairs.original: 撞过南墙的、走过弯路的——投过的项目亏损、认准的商机失利, 而开始怀疑人生。
pairs.english: People who have experienced failed investments or unsuccessful opportunities and have begun to question their direction in life.

pairs.original: 遭遇信任危机, 营销思路想把“流量”变成“留量”, 提升客户黏性的企业主。
pairs.english: Owners facing a trust crisis who want to turn passing traffic into lasting customer relationships and stronger loyalty.

pairs.original: 创始人、董事长、总经理、股东等负责战略决策者。
pairs.english: Founders, chairpersons, general managers, shareholders and others responsible for strategic decisions.

pairs.original: 愿意和企业主同心同德的股东、合伙人。
pairs.english: Shareholders and partners willing to work in alignment with the business owner.

pairs.original: 关注心性成长, 悟性极高的修行人, 不怨天尤人、能认识到一切困局皆因自己眼界、认知的局限等自身格局导致的。
pairs.english: People interested in inner cultivation who are willing to examine the limits of their own perspective rather than blame others. The source presents the belief that personal limitations underlie every predicament; this is the programme’s assertion, not an established explanation of all adversity.

pairs.original: 针对企业主的九大处境
pairs.english: Nine business situations addressed.

pairs.original: 面对百年未有之时代变局，物质过剩，产品同质化，营销陷入瓶颈，市场空间越来越小，利润越来越少，看不到未来的方向，企业该何去何从？
pairs.english: Material abundance, similar products, marketing bottlenecks, shrinking space and margins, and uncertainty about the future direction of the enterprise.

pairs.original: 现有业务盈利能力减弱、模式老化，新的业务增长又没有找到，销售额徘徊不前，找不到突围之路。
pairs.english: A weakening existing business or ageing model, with no clear new source of growth and stagnant sales.

pairs.original: 近年来一直投资失利，项目亏损，导致信心下降，个人能量大不如从前。
pairs.english: Repeated investment losses and declining confidence or personal energy.

pairs.original: 家庭关系、股东、合伙人、核心团队等关系缺乏弹性，无人理解。得不到相应的支持，孤军奋战，内心孤独。
pairs.english: Strained family, shareholder, partner or core-team relationships; lack of understanding and support; and a sense of facing problems alone.

pairs.original: 对孩子的教育、人才的培养问题都很焦虑，不能深刻洞悉人性，无法因材施教、顺势而为。
pairs.english: Anxiety about children’s education and talent development, alongside uncertainty about understanding differences and supporting people appropriately.

pairs.original: 经营模式陈旧，企业管理的方法学过、用过很多，仍没有理想效果。
pairs.english: An outdated operating model and disappointing results despite trying many management methods.

pairs.original: 营销成本、人工成本上涨，利润枯竭，业绩停滞不前。
pairs.english: Rising marketing and labour costs, depleted profits and stalled performance.

pairs.original: 公司发展战略不清晰，高层思想不统一，基层执行不得力。
pairs.english: An unclear company strategy, disagreement at senior levels and ineffective execution.

pairs.original: 发展受限、各种制约、面临转型，不知所措，迷茫困惑。
pairs.english: Constraints on development and confusion about how to navigate a necessary transition.

editorialSections.heading: Translation and interpretation limits
paragraphs: The source is a promotional and philosophical overview. Its strong promises and claims about “energy,” destiny and self-responsibility are preserved as the programme’s language; the translation does not endorse them as scientific or clinical findings.

The five paths, six directions and seven levels are not actually listed. Their headings do not justify inventing a curriculum, a diagnostic ladder or a numerical test. The eight audiences and nine situations above are the lists that were supplied.

title: The CEO operating review: 15 areas of responsibility
summary: Connect executive responsibilities with evidence, decisions and owners across strategy, finance, people and continuity.
takeaway: A review becomes useful when evidence leads to an owned decision and follow-up.
steps: Gather evidence and ask the team
Identify the decision and accountable owner
notes: The supplied poster has no visible creator credit. Its repeated CFO references are not universal role-allocation rules; adapt ownership to the organization. Two overlapping innovation prompts and the repeated risk-identification item are consolidated below, with the full source image available.

ranges.heading: Board, ownership and management boundaries
ranges.introduction: Separate shareholder ownership, board oversight, executive delivery and project/functional management. Exact approvals and responsibilities depend on the organization’s governing documents and jurisdiction.

title: Executive review questions: strategy, friction and opportunity
summary: Use the thirty supplied management prompts to diagnose a decision rather than score the business against an invented benchmark.
takeaway: Give each management question a review period, evidence and a decision context.

ranges.heading: Thirty questions for a management review
ranges.introduction: Work through the questions in relation to a defined planning horizon. “This year” and “third quarter” are source-relative wording, not current forecasts; record the actual date and period in your own review.

title: Venture and funding readiness: questions before the pitch
summary: Examine the problem, market, team, customer economics and reason for financing before choosing a fundraising story.
takeaway: Explain why capital is needed and what customer evidence supports the business case.
notes: These are reflection prompts, not an investor approval checklist or a guarantee that a venture should raise capital.

ranges.heading: Thirty-three questions before seeking capital
ranges.introduction: Choose the questions that fit the business stage and proposed financing. Customer funding, subscription economics, market scope and defensive position are different issues; do not total yes/no answers into a readiness score.

title: Employee-experience conversations: clarity, resources and growth
summary: Discuss working conditions and development with independently written topic guidance, without claiming to administer a validated assessment.
takeaway: Discuss working conditions without inventing an official assessment score.
notes: The supplied twelve prompts follow Gallup Q12 topics and ordering. This page does not reproduce or administer Q12, offer its scores or benchmarks, or claim Gallup validation. Consult the linked owner for the official instrument.

ranges.heading: Twelve themes from the supplied employee prompts

curatedBlocks.text: The supplied notes follow the topic order of Gallup’s Q12. The official source is linked for that instrument; the discussion here is independently worded topic guidance rather than an administered questionnaire or Gallup-validated adaptation.

items: Role clarity: shared expectations for the work.
Resources: access to the tools and conditions needed to contribute.
Strengths: opportunities to use and develop capabilities.
Recognition: credible acknowledgement of useful contributions.
Care and respect: a working relationship in which people matter.
Development support: access to feedback and encouragement.
Voice: a fair way to express ideas and concerns.
Purpose: a clear connection between work and worthwhile outcomes.
Quality: shared commitment to reliable standards.
Progress: conversations about learning and contribution over time.
Growth: opportunities to learn and take on useful challenges.

curatedBlocks.text: Use these as topics for a respectful conversation, not as twelve scored survey items. No employee ranking, diagnostic threshold, benchmark or assurance of anonymity is inferred.

sourceOnly.reason: Owner-identified Q12 wording is retained as provenance; public content uses independent topic explanations without reproducing/administering the instrument.

title: Leadership competencies: describe behaviour before assigning a rating
summary: Organize the supplied competency categories into observable examples and development conversations without an invented overall score.
takeaway: Describe observable behaviour and context before assigning a judgement.

visuals.title: Seven categories, one evidence discipline
rows: A concrete team situation and observed action
An appropriate work sample or explained decision
How assumptions and alternatives were examined
Sustained work and response to feedback
Demonstrated capability relevant to the actual role
visuals.note: Categories are discussion prompts, not weighted scores or permanent labels.

ranges.heading: Seven competency categories and behavioural prompts
ranges.introduction: Ask for observable examples, context and development needs. Some source labels such as “aggressive” are ambiguous; discuss the intended behaviour and its effects rather than rewarding the label. No weighting, validated scale or overall cut-off was supplied.

ranges.heading: Ability, motivation and opportunity
ranges.introduction: This one-line performance model is a prompt to examine skills, willingness and conditions that allow contribution. It does not supply a causal coefficient, validated scoring rule or formula for an employee’s output.

editorialSections.heading: Use evidence instead of a total score
paragraphs: Choose a role and a small number of relevant behaviours. For each, record a concrete example, the work context, what good performance would look like and the support or practice needed. Review changes over time rather than adding unlike categories into a single number.

title: Cross-cultural leadership: compare Hofstede and GLOBE carefully
summary: Keep culture dimensions, reported practices, desired values and leadership expectations distinct from assumptions about individuals.
takeaway: An aggregate cultural comparison cannot determine an individual colleague’s preferences.

visuals.title: Different models, different constructs
rows: Power distance; individualism/collectivism; masculinity/femininity; uncertainty avoidance; long/short-term orientation; indulgence/restraint
Aggregate societal comparisons; not personal abilities or an individual diagnosis
Performance; assertiveness; future; humane; institutional collectivism; in-group collectivism; gender egalitarianism; power distance; uncertainty avoidance
Keep practices (“as is”) distinct from desired values (“should be”)
Charismatic/value-based; team-oriented; participative; humane-oriented; autonomous; self-protective
Separate leadership expectations from the societal dimension list
visuals.note: Historical dimension labels are retained with scope; do not stereotype an individual from a national average.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: Hofstede’s six societal dimensions and GLOBE’s nine societal dimensions plus six leadership dimensions are different constructs. Use group-level comparisons as questions about context, not predictions of an individual employee.

The source’s short/long-term orientation wording is misleading: pragmatic adaptation belongs with long-term orientation in the Hofstede model. Uncertainty avoidance is not simply willingness to take a financial risk. The sourced comparison below keeps the models separate.

editorialSections.heading: Ask before assuming
paragraphs: Hofstede compares aggregate societal dimensions. GLOBE distinguishes reported practices from desired values and separately explores leadership expectations. The scores cannot be swapped between models or used to predict an individual colleague’s preferences. Ask about a real team’s ways of communicating, deciding and resolving disagreement.

title: Team roles and coordination: compare contributions and dysfunctions
summary: Use Belbin, Lencioni and the supplied team distinctions as different discussion lenses rather than a single personality or team score.
takeaway: Development stages, behavioural contributions and team obstacles are different lenses.

references.title: The Table Group's original model overview

ranges.heading: Collaboration, dysfunctions and nine contributions
ranges.introduction: Cooperative/collaborative are used as source distinctions, not universal definitions of every team. Keep the five dysfunctions and nine Belbin contributions separate from the team-development stages already covered elsewhere.

editorialSections.heading: Keep the lenses distinct
paragraphs: Tuckman concerns development over time; Belbin concerns behavioural contributions; Lencioni concerns obstacles to collective work. A person can make several contributions and a team does not need nine people to discuss nine roles. None of these short notes provides a validated local scoring system.

links.label: Review shared goals and team conditions

editorialSections.heading: A contribution vocabulary and an obstacle vocabulary
paragraphs: Belbin’s nine contributions are Resource Investigator, Teamworker, Co-ordinator, Plant, Monitor Evaluator, Specialist, Shaper, Implementer and Completer Finisher. Discuss the behaviours the task needs; a person need not be confined to one role.

Lencioni’s five dysfunctions are absence of trust, fear of conflict, lack of commitment, avoidance of accountability and inattention to results. The constructive discussion concerns admitting difficulties, debating ideas, agreeing commitments, reviewing behaviour and attending to shared outcomes. No diagnostic cut-off is supplied.

title: Leadership models: transformation, service and emergent change
summary: Compare the supplied leadership frameworks by the question each asks and the behaviours it highlights.
takeaway: Ask which behaviours a model highlights and which claims its evidence actually supports.

references.title: Mind Garden, the instrument publisher, explains the components and lineage

ranges.heading: Leadership progression, humility and resolve
ranges.introduction: The supplied progression moves from individual contribution to organizational leadership and includes reflection, debate and accountability. Use it as an attributed framework discussion, not a score proving someone’s level.

ranges.heading: Transformational leadership as a general description
ranges.introduction: The source emphasizes inspiring new approaches. The more specific four-component framework is distinguished later in this guide.

ranges.heading: Transformational and servant-leadership themes
ranges.introduction: The four Bass components and ten Spears characteristics answer different questions and should not be combined into one score. The source’s “rust” wording is a typographical error, not a definition of inspirational motivation.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: The brief attributed systems account proposes disequilibrium, amplifying actions, self-organization and stabilizing feedback. It is not enough to validate a predictive organizational model. Explain the proposed lens without asserting that disruption inevitably creates a desirable new order.

editorialSections.heading: Four components and ten characteristics
paragraphs: Transformational leadership distinguishes idealized influence, inspirational motivation, intellectual stimulation and individualized consideration. Examples are setting an ethical example, connecting work to purpose, questioning assumptions and developing others. This page is separate from any licensed leadership questionnaire.

Spears’s servant-leadership account names listening, empathy, healing, awareness, persuasion, conceptualization, foresight, stewardship, commitment to people’s growth and community. “Healing” is a relational theme here, not a medical claim.

title: Delegation and decision rights: authority with clear handoffs
summary: Distinguish delegation direction, capability, decision ownership and accountability before handing work to someone else.
takeaway: Agree authority, resources, expectations and escalation alongside the assignment.

ranges.heading: Delegation direction and capability
ranges.introduction: Name who owns the decision, who does the work, what resources are available and what an escalation looks like. The source’s cycle and team labels are prompts rather than a complete scheduling or authority procedure.

ranges.heading: Decision ownership, reflection and execution
ranges.introduction: Separate boss-decides, consultation, delegated individual ownership and collective decisions. The DEEP heading has no supplied expansion; retain the stated reflection/data/alternatives/review sequence without inventing its acronym or a validated decision score.

title: Meeting design: decide together or communicate asynchronously?
summary: Choose the interaction needed, the people who can contribute and a clear completion condition before scheduling a meeting.
takeaway: Match the interaction to the required outcome before inviting people.

ranges.heading: Offsite preparation and facilitation
ranges.introduction: Protect the session from ordinary work, prepare participants, choose contributors for insight and allow enough time. Clarify what must be decided rather than treating an offsite itself as an outcome.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: Salary, preparation, travel, delayed delivery and attention are plausible cost categories to estimate for an actual meeting. The source’s 20%, 40%, 50% and 15% assertions and two-days-per-week claim lack a dated sample and should not be presented as current benchmarks.
Decide what must happen synchronously and compare the cost with the expected decision or learning benefit; do not infer a precise cost saving from these unsupported percentages.

ranges.heading: Choose, structure and facilitate the interaction
ranges.introduction: The source distinguishes discussion from broadcast, proposes OPPT (outcome, process, participation, timing), and lists participation techniques. Apply the technique to context: an invitation, break or subgroup can help, whereas attendance penalties or calling on people should not override accessibility or respectful participation.

editorialSections.heading: A compact meeting record
paragraphs: Before: state the required decision or learning outcome, preparation and participants. During: make the process and time boundary clear and invite contributions in an appropriate way. After: record the decision, owner, action, date and anything that needs a separate conversation.

title: Trust and accountability: make commitments observable
summary: Connect clarity, competence, contribution and consistent follow-through without treating trust as a guaranteed financial multiplier.
takeaway: Make commitments reviewable through clear ownership, resources, timing and evidence.

ranges.heading: Seeing problems and accepting feedback
ranges.introduction: Welcome difficult conversations, examine evidence and link an observation to an agreed result. Removing blame does not remove responsibility for repairing a problem.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: The source lists potential effects of trust and practices such as clarity, compassion, competence and consistency. The assertion that low trust doubles business cost has no supplied dataset or model and is not a numerical rule.
The last lines run several labels together. Their themes can support a discussion of contribution and follow-through, but no missing formal taxonomy or causal result is inferred.

editorialSections.heading: Make a commitment reviewable
paragraphs: State what is promised, by whom, with what resources, by when and how a problem can be raised. Review whether the promise was fulfilled and what changed; a general feeling of trust is not a substitute for evidence or appropriate controls.

title: Five ways to describe strategy: plan, pattern, position, perspective and ploy
summary: Use the supplied five-P list to ask whether a strategy is an intention, an observed pattern or a relationship to its environment.
takeaway: Make clear whether strategy means an intention, an observed pattern or a relationship to the environment.

ranges.heading: The supplied five-P vocabulary
ranges.introduction: These are different ways of describing strategy, not five steps that must be completed in order.

title: Why people share: the STEPPS discussion framework
summary: Explore social currency, triggers, emotion, public visibility, practical value and stories when planning shareable communication.
takeaway: Ask why someone would share and what useful value the audience receives.

ranges.heading: The six supplied sharing themes
ranges.introduction: The examples illustrate possible mechanisms to discuss. Their anecdotes do not establish that every airline or platform follows the quoted incentive policy.

editorialSections.heading: Apply the six questions to a real message
paragraphs: Social currency: what does sharing communicate about the person? Triggers: what makes the subject come to mind? Emotion: what response makes people want to pass it on? Public visibility: how can behaviour be observed? Practical value: what useful help is offered? Stories: how does a narrative carry the message? These are planning lenses, not a formula guaranteeing virality.

title: Launching a two-sided platform: eight ways to start participation
summary: Compare the source’s approaches to the chicken-and-egg problem using the first participant group and the value it receives.
takeaway: Provide concrete value for the first participants and a credible bridge to the other side.

references.title: The three book authors' INSEAD article, 29 July 2016

ranges.heading: The eight supplied platform-launch approaches
ranges.introduction: Choose which side receives value first and how that value attracts the next participants. The examples are historical; strategy fit requires a current market and unit-economics check.

editorialSections.heading: What each approach starts with
paragraphs: Follow-the-rabbit demonstrates an already valuable example. Piggyback draws on an existing platform or audience. Seeding supplies initial value or participation. Marquee attracts an important anchor participant. Single-side offers standalone utility before connecting sides. Producer evangelism lets producers bring their audiences. Big-bang adoption concentrates launch attention. Micromarket builds density in a small initial market.

The eight approaches match the authors’ Platform Revolution account in the linked 2016 INSEAD article. Do not confuse platform piggybacking with international-distribution piggybacking; the context and constraints differ.

title: Value selling and misleading offers: examine the examples
summary: Read the collection’s performance-zone labels, dead-donkey story and bundled-offer example as prompts for critical judgment.
takeaway: Read the collection’s performance-zone labels, dead-donkey story and bundled-offer example as prompts for critical judgment.

ranges.heading: Match the offer to the need

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: The source supplies buying/selling and familiarity anecdotes. Their origin and factual details are unverified; some language relies on dated cultural stereotypes. Use the underlying question—does the offer solve the buyer’s actual need?—without presenting these stories as evidence about a group of people.

title: Investing maxims, decision behavior and compounded returns
summary: Read the supplied investment observations as prompts for evidence, cost awareness and goal-focused decisions, with claims separated from financial identities.
takeaway: Read the supplied investment observations as prompts for evidence, cost awareness and goal-focused decisions, with claims separated from financial identities.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: The soybean example illustrates different processing and business models, not investment returns on comparable cash flows. Its dollar amounts, costs, risks and time horizons are unspecified. The claims about rich/poor behaviour and guaranteed effects of mindset are not established by the anecdote.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: The Einstein attribution is unverified. Compounding depends on the rate, time, contributions, costs and risks; the saying does not establish a particular investment outcome.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: This is a rhetorical statement about credit access, not a literal description of every lender’s eligibility or underwriting criteria.

title: Everyday influence: interest, appreciation and listening
summary: Read six interpersonal practices associated in the notes with winning friends and influencing people.
takeaway: Read six interpersonal practices associated in the notes with winning friends and influencing people.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: The source proposes observing presence, voice, nonverbal communication and stories. Avoid assuming that a cue reveals someone’s unconscious state or that a deep voice guarantees authority. Ask for clarification and use respectful, transparent communication.

ranges.heading: Recognition and attentive listening
ranges.introduction: The distinct practice details are pausing, asking for clarification and paraphrasing. Appreciation and approval should remain sincere, rather than be tools for manufacturing dependence.

ranges.heading: Interest, enthusiasm and treating people as important
ranges.introduction: Use sincere appreciation and careful attention; do not confuse making people feel valued with agreeing to every request.

ranges.heading: Practical ways to make and maintain contact
ranges.introduction: The additional examples concern introductions, pronunciation, personal follow-up and considerate contact. Adapt them to privacy and the relationship rather than collecting personal details unnecessarily.

coveredBy.reason: Existing interest, appreciation and listening principles already cover respecting differences and avoiding unsolicited reform of others.
The existing canonical reading covers making others feel important; the Mary Kay attribution is unverified and adds no distinct practice.

title: Clear communication: the seven Cs and visual presentation
summary: Connect coherent, clear, concise, correct, complete, courteous and concrete messages with the supplied presentation-design prompts.
takeaway: Connect coherent, clear, concise, correct, complete, courteous and concrete messages with the supplied presentation-design prompts.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: Specific verbs can make an action clearer, but forceful language is not automatically more accurate. Expressions such as “as my client” or “with your approval” should follow actual agreement, not manufacture consent. Positive language must leave room for honest disagreement and uncertainty.

takeaway: Explore the two-minute rule, GTD, a daily habit chain, Parkinson’s Law and the big-rocks approach.

paragraphs: The Johari Window is associated with Joseph Luft and Harry Ingham. A later author-written account discusses areas known or unknown to oneself and to others, and cautions against forced disclosure. The earlier matrix in this guide has its own supplied labels; it has not been silently replaced by a canonical Johari diagram. The original 1955 proceedings were not independently accessed.

title: Customer economics: churn, acquisition, retention and recurring revenue
summary: Connect customer measures with acquisition cost, recurring-revenue movements and unit economics.
takeaway: Connect customer measures with acquisition cost, recurring-revenue movements and unit economics.

review.status: Read the source with these limits
paragraphs: Define the cohort, period and numerator before using any rate. Profit divided by customers is profit per customer for the stated period; it is not automatically lifetime value. Acquisition cost uses the matching acquisition spend and new customers acquired.

The notes use CPC for both click and customer costs. Label cost per click separately from customer acquisition cost. The LV/CPC expression is a scaled ratio with unclear bases, not an automatically valid cash-on-cash investment return.

Unique visitors divided by matching reach is a rate if the populations and time windows align, not a volume count. The greater-than symbol between click and acquisition costs does not define a conversion formula. Source data and attribution rules are needed before building a calculator.
